items.title: Import and integrity-bind the approved dynamic validation design record
items.context: Create the repository decision record from the supplied UTF-8 plan, preserving Sections 1 through 27.6, the payload-prefix audit envelope, the source SHA-256 db16fccb5af01d296362e0d5e882e69922525b3341e5ce1a68376a352865c68a, and the DYN-1 observe-only versus DYN-3 authority distinction. Record B-38b7 only as stale documentation-only zombie history.
items.userSees: The repository contains the approved design record with a reproducible payload digest and authority boundary.

happy.desc: Run the decision-record integrity check against docs/requirements/decisions/story-aware-dynamic-validation-execution-plan.md and assert selector `sourceSha256=db16fccb5af01d296362e0d5e882e69922525b3341e5ce1a68376a352865c68a`; Sections 1 through 27.6 and the payload-prefix audit envelope are present byte-for-byte. WHY: the approved plan is the source contract, not an approximate summary.

Run the documentation navigation/link check and assert selectors `DYN-1=observe-only`, `DYN-3=TEST authority`, and `B-38b7=stale documentation-only`; NAV points to the new decision record and does not promote the zombie story. WHY: authority boundaries and discoverability must be user-visible.

edge.desc: Recompute the digest after UTF-8 line-ending, Unicode, or payload-prefix changes and assert `payload digest mismatch` with no imported record accepted; a historical 107/110 count or prose-only copy is not substituted. WHY: encoding and normalization drift must not silently change the approved contract.

Check a record with a missing section, duplicate section heading, or truncated Section 27.6 and assert the import reports the exact missing/duplicate boundary and remains non-authoritative. WHY: partial documents cannot seed implementation decisions.

adversarial.desc: Flip one byte in the decision payload or replace the source SHA-256, run the tamper self-test, and assert nonzero-equivalent rejection before any decision-record approval or gate evidence. WHY: tampering must fail closed.

Inject an active B-38b7 authority claim or label DYN-1 as TEST authority, run the plan-review selector, and assert rejection with the DYN-1 observe-only/DYN-3 authority distinction intact. WHY: stale history and observe mode must not widen authority.

items.title: Discover and freeze the current-main validation inventory and implementation boundary
items.context: Derive current N and inventory digest instead of using historical 107 or 110 command examples. Characterize actual full-plan identities, command order, scheduler, executor, resource claims, focused validation, evidence reuse, build binding, lifecycle, process/runtime facts, material hashes, whole-repository scanners, risk tiers, and serial/resource baselines. Record current-main touchpoints plus a high-risk decision with three pre-mortems.
items.userSees: Validation discovery reports a current-main inventory count and digest and labels historical counts non-authoritative.

happy.desc: Current main discovery emits a complete inventory with one stable command ID per configured validation command and a frozen inventory digest.
The characterization report records serial and resource-aware full results, command order, risk tiers, scanner classes, and implementation touchpoints.

edge.desc: A command with a missing timeout, resource claim, or historical duration is retained in the inventory and classified conservatively rather than silently omitted.
Historical 107/110 command snapshots cannot change the kickoff-derived N or inventory digest.

adversarial.desc: Adding a duplicate ID, catalogless command, or unknown configured command fails inventory construction before selection.
A shared lifecycle, scheduler, executor, catalog, process-fact, or validation-config change is classified as full-risk during characterization.

items.title: Implement the canonical Story change manifest and dual-revision impact graph
items.context: Extract a shared changed-file resolver used by freshness and dynamic selection. Sign a merge-base-to-HEAD manifest that records added, modified, deleted, renamed old/new paths, scope violations, verificationIntent pins, packages, process facts, and capabilities. Build content-addressed base and HEAD graphs with static and literal dynamic imports, package exports, CLI registries, generated bindings, bounded reverse dependencies, delete-through-base lookup, both rename paths, and conservative bindings for nonliteral relations.
items.userSees: Dynamic validation prints exact changed files, rename/deletion impact reasons, and mandatory scope escalation.

happy.desc: The signed Story change manifest and shared resolver agree on the current merge-base-to-HEAD file set and selection inputs.

edge.desc: Deleted paths resolve dependents through the base graph and renamed paths union old-base and new-HEAD reverse dependents.

adversarial.desc: An unmapped, protected, explicit-exclusion, or out-of-scope actual change remains in the manifest and forces full escalation.

items.title: Implement deterministic three-state selection, full escalation, and signed manifests
items.context: Initialize all inventory rows as unverified. Additively select always, verificationIntent pins, changed-test consumers, certified closure triggers, dual-graph dependents, facts, capabilities, and only snapshot-bound historical recommendations. Enforce full-only, whole-repository, never-reuse, scope/protected/exclusion, and all mandatory escalation semantics. Convert uncertainty to execution or full escalation, prove singleton-union monotonicity, require execute union reuse equal inventory and zero unverified/uncovered/unmapped, and sign a source-build-bound selection manifest. Do not use heuristic/set-cover subtraction or upgrade focused receipts.
items.userSees: The CLI lists inventory, executed, reused, unverified, uncovered, unmapped changes, per-command reasons, escalation reasons, and a selection digest.

happy.desc: The selection manifest deterministically partitions the complete inventory into execute and admissible reuse rows with zero unverified, uncovered, and unmapped rows.

edge.desc: Adding a changed file, process fact, capability, or pin can only add selected commands and never subtract a singleton contribution.

adversarial.desc: Incomplete closure, systemic ambiguity, impacted full-only command, scope violation, or catalog drift converts uncertainty to execution or complete-plan escalation.

items.title: Run DYN-2 shadow reuse and prove complete-plan oracle equivalence
items.context: In shadow mode execute and verify the dynamic subset, then execute the complete plan as sole authority. Persist executed/reused/unverified/uncovered accounting, compare each command and final verdict, prove failures(full) are a subset of executed(dynamic), exercise receipt rejection and cleanup/residue controls, and retain full runs as canonical baselines. Dynamic evidence may not pass TEST or DONE in shadow.
items.userSees: Shadow mode displays its ledger and the following full-oracle comparison without claiming TEST or DONE authority.

happy.desc: Shadow mode executes and verifies the dynamic subset, then the complete plan, and records per-command and final verdict equivalence with the full plan authoritative.

edge.desc: A reused row that becomes unavailable or a dynamic command failure is surfaced in the comparison ledger without hiding the full oracle result.

adversarial.desc: A full-plan failure outside dynamic executed rows or any failure reused as PASS is detected as a false-negative soundness failure.

items.title: Complete replay, fault-injection, mutation, and enforcement evidence
items.context: Replay 30 to 50 historical Stories across docs, local, shared, lifecycle, facts, validation runtime, package/config, rename/delete, intentional failure, and test-only classes. Require failures(full, Story) subset-of executed(dynamic, Story). Run FI-1 through FI-5 for every applicable catalog entry and all Section 20 mutation rows with durable named receipts. Run three alternating paired current-HEAD experiments, report medians, cache, utilization, overlap, and residue, and block DYN-3 until every Section 19 threshold passes.

happy.desc: The replay campaign covers 30 to 50 representative Story classes and emits per-story/per-command evidence showing full failures are a subset of dynamic execute rows.

edge.desc: FI-1 through FI-5 and the Section 20 mutation rows each produce a durable named fail-closed receipt, including deleted/renamed and whole-repository cases.

adversarial.desc: Missing one catalog mutant, false-negative replay, absent paired run, nonzero undeclared runtime inputs, or residual artifact blocks enforcement even if a generic suite is green.

items.title: Implement DYN-4 weighted LPT scheduling and resource-safe selected execution
items.context: For execute rows only, add CPU weights, expected P50s, stable wave then longest-processing-time ordering, refined dist reader/writer and other resource claims, capacity admission, and timeline persistence. adversarial.desc: Mutations removing CPU-weight enforcement, writer exclusivity, or drain barriers are rejected and cannot produce an authoritative PASS.

adversarial.desc: Deleting a shard, duplicating a case, routing a case incorrectly, substituting static PASS, or leaving temporary/process/ticket/quarantine residue is rejected.
